instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines "communicates directly with" as contact "in person or by telephone, telegraph, letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or other electronic means of communication," which covers oral (in person/telephone), written (letter), electronic, phone calls, and emails, but not virtual, organising meetings, or events.

"Person" is defined broadly to include individuals, corporations, associations, firms, partnerships, etc., and §305.003 requires registration of any such person making expenditures or receiving compensation to lobby (including in-house regular employees per §305.003(b)); §305.003(b-1) excludes government/judicial/legislative/executive officers and political subdivision employees, so public entities and government agencies are not included.

The definitions section in §305.002 does not contain any definition of "public entity"; the chapter defines "person," "member of legislative branch," "member of executive branch," etc., but not "public entity."

The statute sets monetary thresholds (not less than $200/quarter in expenditures or compensation) and a time threshold (not more than 26 hours per quarter under (b-3)) below which registration is not required, functioning as materiality/de minimis exemptions.

The definition of lobbying covers communicating directly with "a member of the legislative or executive branch" to influence legislation or administrative action, and "member of the executive branch" includes officers of any state agency/department/office of the executive branch (which encompasses the governor).

Targets include members of the legislative branch (members, candidates, officers, and employees of the legislature/legislative committees) and members of the executive branch (officers and employees of any state agency, department, or office in the executive branch), covering legislators, senior officials, and staff.

Same as row_005: the lobbying definition covers direct communications with members of the legislative or executive branch (including officers of executive branch offices, which includes the Governor).

Same as row_005/007: §305.003(a) requires registration for communications with members of the legislative or executive branch, and §305.002(4) defines executive branch members as officers/employees of any state agency, department, or office in the executive branch.
Same as row_005/007/008: the statute covers communications with both legislative and executive branch members including the governor as an executive officer.

Targets include legislative branch members (members, officers, employees) and executive branch officers/employees of any state agency, department, or office — covering legislators, senior officials, and administrative staff.

The statute expressly states that §305.003(a)(2) "does not require a member of the judicial, legislative, or executive branch of state government or an officer or employee of a political subdivision of the state to register," so elected officials and public appointees are exempt from the registration requirement.

The statute addresses public employees: §305.003(b-1) exempts political subdivision officers/employees but covers quasi-governmental agency employees, §305.0051 authorizes the commission to require public officers/employees to file disclosure, and §305.003 sets compensation ($200/quarter), expenditure ($200/quarter), and time (26 hours/quarter) standards for registration.

The definitions and registration triggers in §305.002 and §305.003 rely on activities (direct communication to influence legislation/administrative action) and compensation/expenditure thresholds, not on any concept of public charter or special government protection.

The statutory definitions of who must register turn on conduct (direct communication to influence) and compensation/expenditure thresholds; ownership is not used as a criterion in the definition of a lobbyist.
The definition of lobbyist depends on activities and dollar/time thresholds (e.g., $200 per quarter, 26 hours per quarter), not on the structure or composition of revenue of the entity.
